sources.label: AOSP: generic boot partition architecture
sources.scope: Defines launch-versus-upgrade placement of the GKI kernel, generic ramdisk, init_boot, vendor_boot recovery resources, and dedicated recovery images.

sources.label: AOSP: vendor boot partitions
sources.scope: Defines vendor_boot header versions, vendor ramdisks, DTB placement, bootconfig, A/B protection, and the relationship between boot and vendor_boot.

sources.label: AOSP: boot image header versions
sources.scope: Defines boot image header versions zero through four and distinguishes the version-four GKI boot_signature from device-specific Verified Boot.

sources.label: AOSP: Android partition roles
sources.scope: Defines core system and vendor partition roles, including boot, init_boot, system_dlkm, vendor_boot, and dedicated or ramdisk-based recovery.

sources.label: AOSP: DTB image placement
sources.scope: Defines version-dependent DTB placement in vendor_boot, boot, a standalone partition, or an image appended to the kernel.

sources.label: AOSP: DTB and DTBO partition selection
sources.scope: Defines DTB and DTBO table structure plus bootloader selection using hardware identifiers such as board ID, revision, custom values, and SoC identity.

sources.label: AOSP: implement dynamic partitions
sources.scope: Defines super metadata, logical partition mapping and sizing, physical bootloader-readable partitions, launch versus retrofit layouts, and chained AVB handling.

sources.label: AOSP: GKI system_dlkm partition
sources.scope: Defines system_dlkm as a dynamic partition and requires GKI modules to be built and updated with their compatible GKI.

sources.label: AOSP: vendor_dlkm and odm_dlkm partitions
sources.scope: Defines vendor and ODM kernel-module partitions, their placement inside super, dependencies on vendor_boot modules, mount order, and A/B update membership.

sources.label: AOSP: loadable kernel modules
sources.scope: Defines verified module locations, recovery-mode availability, kernel-module version checks, symbol CRC matching, and recompile requirements after ABI changes.

sources.label: AOSP: Verified Boot chain and rollback protection
sources.scope: Defines verification of boot, device tree, system, vendor and related data, boot-time versus runtime failures, and per-partition rollback protection.

sources.label: AOSP: build Pixel kernels
sources.scope: Documents Pixel 6-family vendor-ramdisk build coupling and the Pixel 7-and-later vendor_kernel_boot split for listed Google kernel-development targets.

records.title: init_boot presence follows launch architecture, not current Android alone
records.summary: Devices launching with Android 13 move the generic ramdisk from boot into init_boot, while devices upgraded from Android 12 can retain their Android 12 boot architecture. A current Android 13-or-later version therefore cannot identify the correct ramdisk or recovery target by itself.
symptoms: A guide says to patch boot but the package contains init_boot
A device running Android 13 or later has no init_boot partition
Root or recovery image target is uncertain
diagnostic_steps: Record the device's original Android launch version separately from its current Android version.
Inventory the exact boot, init_boot, vendor_boot, recovery, recovery_a, and recovery_b partition names without writing them.
Inspect the matching factory or maintainer package to see which boot-chain images it actually supplies.
fix_steps: Use the exact device and build guide whose partition target agrees with the observed launch architecture and partition inventory.
If launch history or partition presence is unknown, stop before patching or flashing any candidate image.
expected_outcomes: ROMVERSE distinguishes boot-target uncertainty from a missing or damaged partition.
compatibility: Devices upgraded to a newer Android release without changing their launch partition architecture
known_incompatibility: Current Android version alone is not sufficient evidence
Legacy non-GKI devices can use different recovery-as-boot arrangements
recovery_routes: Return to the exact OEM factory package or maintained device guide and rebuild Device DNA

scope.scope_note: Platform architecture rule. The actual target remains exact-device, original-launch-version, partition-map, and build scoped.

records.title: GKI boot image contents change at the Android 13 launch boundary
records.summary: For Android 12 launch GKI layouts, boot contains the GKI kernel and generic ramdisk. For devices launching with Android 13, boot contains the GKI kernel while init_boot contains the generic ramdisk. An upgraded device can keep the older layout.
symptoms: Patched boot image has no expected ramdisk effect
Unpacked boot image contains a kernel but no generic ramdisk
Package contains both boot and init_boot
diagnostic_steps: Inspect image headers and contents offline before deciding which image owns the generic ramdisk.
Compare the result with original launch version and the exact factory package partition list.
fix_steps: Choose a device-specific workflow that targets the observed ramdisk-bearing image.
Do not copy a boot-patching target from a neighboring model or from a device that merely runs the same Android version.
expected_outcomes: The selected guide agrees with the image that actually contains the generic ramdisk.
compatibility: GKI devices using boot image header version 3 or 4
known_incompatibility: Non-GKI and legacy recovery-as-boot devices require their own partition map
recovery_routes: Restore the coherent unmodified boot-chain images from the exact build if an incorrect target was used

scope.scope_note: GKI architecture distinction. Original launch version and actual image contents decide the layout.

records.title: vendor_boot must remain coherent with the kernel and platform build
records.summary: vendor_boot can carry the vendor ramdisk, device-specific boot parameters, DTB, kernel modules, recovery resources, and bootconfig. The bootloader combines it with boot, so a vendor_boot image from another device or build can fail before Android starts even when boot itself is valid.
symptoms: Bootloop begins after replacing vendor_boot
Kernel starts but first-stage init or hardware initialization fails
Recovery no longer starts after a vendor_boot change
diagnostic_steps: Record hashes and build provenance for boot, init_boot, vendor_boot, DTB, and the current slot.
Inspect the vendor_boot header version, ramdisk fragments, DTB presence, and bootconfig offline.
Confirm the source package explicitly supports the exact model, codename, build, and boot-header layout.
fix_steps: Restore a coherent boot-chain set from one exact OEM or maintainer build rather than mixing individual images.
Keep the device unlocked or locked state unchanged while diagnosis is incomplete; this record grants no relock authority.
expected_outcomes: boot and vendor_boot describe the same device-specific boot environment and Android platform build.
compatibility: Devices implementing vendor_boot header version 3 or 4
known_incompatibility: Some older devices keep vendor-specific boot data in boot or another layout
vendor_boot from a related model is not interchangeable
recovery_routes: Exact-build full OTA or OEM factory restore
Restore the untouched boot-chain backup when verified

scope.scope_note: Platform-level coherence diagnosis; exact image compatibility remains device, build, header-version, slot, and AVB scoped.

records.title: Generic and vendor ramdisks require a compatible concatenated format
records.summary: On GKI boot flows the vendor ramdisk and generic ramdisk are concatenated for early userspace. Their compression and header architecture are build-time compatibility facts, so a separately rebuilt or borrowed ramdisk can be structurally valid yet incompatible with the boot flow.
symptoms: Boot fails during ramdisk decompression or first-stage init
Individually unpackable boot images fail only when combined on device
diagnostic_steps: Inspect the compression format and header version of each ramdisk-bearing image offline.
Verify all ramdisk fragments originated from the same supported target build or documented compatible build set.
fix_steps: Recreate or restore the boot-chain images with the compression and layout expected by the exact device build.
Do not convert compression formats or concatenate fragments based only on a generic guide.
expected_outcomes: The bootloader and kernel can consume the complete ramdisk stream in the expected order and format.
compatibility: GKI layouts that combine vendor and generic ramdisks
known_incompatibility: A ramdisk that works on one header layout is not proof for another
recovery_routes: Restore untouched boot, init_boot, and vendor_boot images from one exact build

scope.scope_note: Applies to concatenated GKI ramdisk architectures; the expected compression and fragment order are device-build configuration.

records.title: Recovery mode does not prove a dedicated recovery partition exists
records.summary: Android devices may use a standalone recovery partition, slotted recovery_a and recovery_b partitions, or recovery resources carried by boot, init_boot, and vendor_boot. A working recovery menu therefore does not prove that flashing recovery is a valid partition operation.
symptoms: Fastboot reports no recovery partition
A recovery image guide disagrees with the observed partition map
Device boots recovery but has no recovery block device
diagnostic_steps: Inventory recovery, recovery_a, recovery_b, boot, init_boot, and vendor_boot without changing them.
Check whether the device is A/B and whether the exact device configuration uses dedicated recovery or recovery resources in a boot ramdisk.
Confirm the maintained installation guide names the same recovery architecture.
fix_steps: Use only the recovery installation or temporary-boot method documented for the exact partition map.
If no dedicated recovery partition exists, do not invent one or redirect the image to boot or init_boot without explicit exact-device guidance.
expected_outcomes: Missing recovery is classified as an architecture fact rather than immediate partition damage.
compatibility: Dedicated recovery and ramdisk-based recovery layouts
known_incompatibility: Partition names and recovery placement vary by device and launch architecture
recovery_routes: Use the exact OEM recovery, full OTA, or maintainer-documented temporary boot route

scope.scope_note: Architecture diagnosis only. Presence of recovery mode is not partition-write authority.

records.title: Boot image header version is a parser compatibility boundary
records.summary: Android boot header versions changed from version 0 through version 4, and the bootloader must parse the declared version correctly. An image built with the wrong header structure, page assumptions, or recovery fields can be rejected or fail before userspace even when its filename is boot.img.
symptoms: Bootloader rejects a boot image as invalid
Image flashes but never reaches kernel or ramdisk
Repacked image size or offsets differ unexpectedly
diagnostic_steps: Read the boot image header version, sizes, page size where applicable, and section offsets offline.
Compare the parsed structure with the exact device's launch-era boot-image requirements and factory image.
fix_steps: Rebuild with the exact header version and layout documented by the device tree or restore the unmodified exact-build image.
Do not select a header version solely from the current Android release.
expected_outcomes: The bootloader parses every image section at the expected location.
compatibility: Android boot image header versions 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4
known_incompatibility: Header version 3 does not carry legacy recovery DTBO or recovery ACPIO fields
Current Android version alone does not prove the required header
recovery_routes: Restore the exact-build factory boot-chain image

scope.scope_note: Image-format diagnosis. Required header version is tied to the device implementation and launch architecture.

records.title: Version-four boot_signature is not the device AVB signature
records.summary: The boot_signature field in boot header version 4 is used for GKI certification and VTS. It is not the device-specific Verified Boot signature; OEMs still sign boot for the device AVB trust chain. Passing one check does not prove the other.
symptoms: A version-four image passes GKI inspection but the device rejects it
Boot verification fails despite a present boot_signature
diagnostic_steps: Identify whether the reported failure is GKI boot_signature validation or device AVB verification.
Record the device root of trust, vbmeta descriptors, boot hash, rollback indexes, and lock state without changing them.
fix_steps: Restore a boot image and vbmeta chain signed for the exact device and build.
Do not disable verification or substitute blank vbmeta as a generic response to this distinction.
expected_outcomes: GKI certification evidence and device trust-chain evidence are reported separately.
compatibility: GKI devices using boot image header version 4
known_incompatibility: A valid boot_signature alone is not device boot authorization
recovery_routes: Exact-build signed full OTA or factory image

scope.scope_note: Applies to header-version-four GKI images; exact AVB keys, descriptors, and lock policy remain device-build scoped.

records.title: DTB location changes across Android boot architectures
records.summary: A DTB may be inside vendor_boot on Android 11 GKI devices, inside boot on Android 10 layouts, or in a standalone partition or kernel-appended image on Android 9-and-earlier designs. Searching only for dtb.img can therefore misdiagnose a valid device layout as missing.
symptoms: Factory package has no standalone dtb.img
A repacked image loses the device tree
Kernel does not initialize the board after a boot image change
diagnostic_steps: Inspect vendor_boot, boot, standalone dtb partitions, and kernel image contents according to the exact launch architecture.
Record the DTB index or selection metadata exposed by the bootloader and compare it with the device board identity.
fix_steps: Restore the DTB in the location and format required by the exact device build.
Do not extract a DTB from one layout and flash it as a standalone partition on another.
expected_outcomes: The bootloader supplies the kernel with the correct device tree for the board.
compatibility: Android devices using DTB-based hardware description
known_incompatibility: DTB placement is not universal across Android versions or devices
recovery_routes: Restore the exact-build boot, vendor_boot, DTB, or complete factory package as dictated by the observed layout

scope.scope_note: Placement rule spans several launch architectures; exact board and build determine the valid DTB and location.

records.title: DTBO selection must match the exact board identity and revision
records.summary: DTBO tables can carry board ID, board revision, SoC ID, and custom hardware selectors that the bootloader uses to choose an overlay. A DTBO from a related model or hardware revision can be well-formed yet select the wrong hardware description.
symptoms: Device stops before Android after replacing dtbo
Display, touch, storage, radio, or other board hardware fails after boot
Bootloader cannot select a valid overlay
diagnostic_steps: Dump the DTBO table offline and record every entry's ID, revision, custom values, and compatible properties.
Compare the selected entry with confirmed board, SoC, and hardware-revision evidence from Device DNA.
Verify the DTBO hash and build provenance against the rest of the boot chain.
fix_steps: Use only the DTBO supplied for the exact device board and coherent build.
If board revision cannot be confirmed, restore the exact factory DTBO instead of testing neighboring variants.
expected_outcomes: The bootloader selects an overlay whose hardware identifiers match the physical device.
compatibility: Devices using Android DTB or DTBO table images
known_incompatibility: Marketing-name similarity does not establish overlay compatibility
Entry order or ID assumptions from another build are unsafe
recovery_routes: Restore exact-build dtbo and the coherent boot-chain set

scope.scope_note: Hardware-selection diagnosis; exact board identity, revision, table entry, build, and AVB chain determine compatibility.

records.title: Dynamic system partitions are logical mappings inside super
records.summary: On dynamic-partition devices, super metadata names and maps logical partitions such as system, vendor, product, system_ext, and odm. They need not appear as independent GPT partitions, while bootloader-read partitions such as boot, dtbo, and vbmeta remain physical.
symptoms: GPT listing does not show system or vendor
Recovery block paths differ from the physical partition table
Fastboot bootloader mode reports a logical partition missing
diagnostic_steps: Record super-partition identity, logical metadata, current slot, partition groups, and whether Fastboot is userspace fastbootd.
Separate a valid logical partition from a corrupt or unreadable super metadata table.
Keep physical bootloader partitions separate from logical operating-system partitions in the Device DNA map.
fix_steps: Use fastbootd or the exact OEM update path only when the device guide requires logical-partition access.
Do not create GPT entries for logical partitions or assume their absence from GPT means they were erased.
expected_outcomes: ROMVERSE identifies whether a named partition is physical, logical, absent, or hidden by the current mode.
known_incompatibility: Legacy fixed-partition devices do not use super logical mappings
boot, dtbo, and vbmeta cannot be ordinary dynamic partitions because the bootloader reads them
recovery_routes: Exact-build full OTA or OEM factory package capable of reconstructing coherent super metadata

scope.scope_note: Dynamic-partition architecture. The logical set, groups, slot metadata, and sizes remain exact-device and build scoped.

records.title: Launch and retrofit dynamic-partition layouts have different super assumptions
records.summary: Devices launching with dynamic partitions place A/B slot handling inside one super partition, while retrofitted devices can retain different physical and metadata arrangements. Package scripts, super images, group budgets, and suffix assumptions must match the device's actual implementation.
symptoms: A super image or script expects super_a or super_b but the device exposes super
Logical metadata loads for one slot but not the expected layout
Repartition instructions disagree with the factory partition table
error_codes: Invalid sparse file format at header magic
diagnostic_steps: Determine whether dynamic partitions were present at launch or added by an upgrade.
Record physical super names, metadata slot count, logical groups, device slot topology, and the package's expected layout.
fix_steps: Use only a super image or update package built for the observed launch-or-retrofit layout.
Stop before repartitioning when the package and Device DNA disagree about physical super naming or group budgets.
expected_outcomes: The package's super metadata model agrees with the device's physical and logical layout.
known_incompatibility: A launch-device super image is not generic retrofit media
Group size limits differ across A/B, Virtual A/B, retrofit A/B, and non-A/B layouts
recovery_routes: Restore the exact OEM partition table and complete factory package through the documented service path

scope.scope_note: Layout compatibility boundary only; no generic repartition operation is declared.

records.title: system_dlkm modules must match the exact GKI build
records.summary: system_dlkm contains Google GKI modules inside super. AOSP states that these modules are compatible only with the GKI they were built with and that no ABI stability exists between a GKI and its GKI modules, so boot and system_dlkm must be built and updated together.
symptoms: Kernel boots but required GKI modules do not load
First-stage mount or hardware initialization fails after changing boot
A mixed kernel package bootloops before Android completes
diagnostic_steps: Record the kernel release, boot hash, system_dlkm hash, module vermagic, module dependencies, and source build.
Compare system_dlkm and boot provenance; matching Android version or security patch label alone is insufficient.
Inspect kernel logs for module version, symbol CRC, dependency, or signature-class failures.
fix_steps: Restore boot and system_dlkm from one compatible exact-device GKI build set.
Do not copy individual modules from a nearby kernel or treat CONFIG_MODVERSIONS as permission to ignore an ABI break.
prerequisites: Exact boot and system_dlkm build provenance
expected_outcomes: Required GKI modules load against the kernel they were built with.
compatibility: Devices launching with Android 13 or later, which AOSP requires to include system_dlkm
known_incompatibility: A same-version kernel label does not prove module compatibility
Legacy devices may store modules in vendor, ODM, or ramdisks instead
recovery_routes: Restore the coherent kernel and system_dlkm images from the exact OEM or maintainer build

scope.scope_note: GKI module coherence rule. Exact kernel and module build identity is required; current Android version is not a substitute.

records.title: vendor_dlkm and odm_dlkm are boot-chain compatibility inputs
records.summary: vendor_dlkm and odm_dlkm are logical partitions inside super that provide vendor and ODM kernel modules. Their modules can depend on modules from vendor_boot and are mounted during first-stage init, so mixing these partitions across builds can break storage, display, radio, or other hardware initialization.
symptoms: Android starts without one or more hardware subsystems
First-stage init cannot load vendor modules
Bootloop begins after changing vendor_dlkm, odm_dlkm, vendor_boot, or the kernel
diagnostic_steps: Record hashes and build provenance for boot, vendor_boot, vendor_dlkm, odm_dlkm, vendor, and odm.
Inspect modules.load, modules.dep, vermagic, missing symbols, and first-stage mount results.
Confirm that A/B slot suffixes and super metadata select the intended module partitions.
fix_steps: Restore the kernel, vendor_boot, vendor_dlkm, odm_dlkm, vendor, and odm components as the exact package defines them.
Do not repair a missing module by downloading an isolated .ko from another build.
expected_outcomes: Vendor and ODM modules mount and load with compatible dependencies for the selected slot.
compatibility: Android 11-and-later devices implementing vendor_dlkm or odm_dlkm
known_incompatibility: Not every device has separate vendor_dlkm or odm_dlkm partitions
Recovery-required modules must be available in the recovery ramfs rather than only vendor or ODM
recovery_routes: Exact-build full OTA or factory restore of the coherent vendor and kernel set

scope.scope_note: Module-partition diagnosis for devices that actually expose these logical partitions; exact dependencies are device and build scoped.

records.title: Recovery cannot depend on modules available only after Android mounts vendor
records.summary: Kernel modules required to boot recovery must be present in the recovery ramfs. A module located only in vendor or ODM might work in full Android yet leave recovery without storage, touch, display, decryption support, or ADB because those partitions are not available in the same way during recovery startup.
symptoms: Android boots but recovery has no touch or storage
Recovery cannot mount partitions that normal Android can mount
Recovery ADB or hardware support disappears after repacking
diagnostic_steps: Collect recovery kernel logs and list the modules available in its ramfs without modifying the image.
Compare recovery-required module dependencies with modules stored only in vendor, odm, vendor_dlkm, or odm_dlkm.
Check whether recovery resources belong in a dedicated recovery image or vendor_boot for this architecture.
fix_steps: Use a recovery image or vendor_boot recovery ramdisk built for the exact kernel and device layout.
Do not add isolated modules unless the exact maintained build configuration and dependency set are available.
expected_outcomes: Recovery loads every module needed before vendor and ODM are available.
compatibility: Devices using loadable modules for recovery-mode hardware
known_incompatibility: Successful module loading in normal Android does not prove recovery availability
recovery_routes: Restore exact-build recovery, vendor_boot, boot, or init_boot images according to the device layout

scope.scope_note: Recovery-mode module diagnosis; exact ramdisk ownership and module set depend on the device boot architecture.

records.title: AVB failures require restoring the described partition chain coherently
records.summary: Verified Boot authenticates the executable code and device data used by the boot flow, including boot, device tree, system, vendor, and partitions delegated through chained vbmeta descriptors. Repair must follow the actual descriptors and rollback indexes instead of assuming vbmeta alone caused the failure.
symptoms: Red corruption screen after mixing partition images
A previously booting locked device rejects one or more restored images
dm-verity causes restart or EIO mode
error_codes: Hash of data does not match digest in descriptor
diagnostic_steps: Read vbmeta and chained descriptors offline to enumerate every protected partition and key relationship.
Record hashes, build provenance, slot, verified-boot state, root-of-trust fingerprint where exposed, and per-partition rollback indexes.
Separate boot-time hash rejection from runtime dm-verity corruption and from kernel-module incompatibility.
fix_steps: Restore the complete descriptor-defined set from one exact signed build or use the signed full OTA or OEM recovery path.
Do not use blank vbmeta, disable verification, or relock as a generic fix. Those actions can hide evidence or make an incompatible chain unbootable.
expected_outcomes: Every protected partition matches its signed descriptor and accepted rollback index.
known_incompatibility: A matching vbmeta image does not compensate for a mismatched boot, DTBO, system, vendor, or chained vbmeta partition
Unlocked-state behavior does not prove safe relock compatibility
recovery_routes: Signed full OTA
Exact OEM factory restore
OEM service route when the trust chain or rollback boundary cannot be satisfied

scope.scope_note: Trust-chain recovery principle. The descriptors on the exact device determine the protected set; no verification-disable or relock operation is authorized.

records.title: Pixel 6-family vendor ramdisk must match the Android platform build
records.summary: AOSP warns that Pixel 6, Pixel 6 Pro, and Pixel 6a kernel repositories can contain a prebuilt vendor ramdisk that does not match the platform build on the device. The documented usual result is an SELinux failure that prevents boot.
symptoms: Pixel 6-family device stops booting after a kernel or vendor_boot change
SELinux failure occurs before Android reaches the home screen
Kernel build used its repository prebuilt vendor ramdisk
diagnostic_steps: Confirm the model and codename is Pixel 6 oriole, Pixel 6 Pro raven, or Pixel 6a bluejay.
Compare the vendor ramdisk source build with the Android platform build currently installed.
Record boot, dtbo, vendor_boot or vendor_boot:dlkm, vendor_dlkm, and slot provenance.
fix_steps: Use the vendor ramdisk from the exact supported Pixel factory build or restore the complete matching factory image set.
Do not transfer the Pixel 7-and-later vendor_kernel_boot layout to this family.
prerequisites: Complete backup or factory restore route
expected_outcomes: The Pixel 6-family vendor ramdisk and platform build carry compatible SELinux and early-boot content.
known_incompatibility: Pixel 7 and later listed development targets split kernel artifacts into vendor_kernel_boot
A repository prebuilt ramdisk is not proof of platform compatibility
recovery_routes: Android Flash Tool back-to-public or exact factory image restore

scope.scope_note: Official Pixel kernel-development boundary for the Pixel 6 family. Exact platform build matching is mandatory; this is diagnosis, not flash authority.

records.title: Listed Pixel 7-and-later targets keep kernel artifacts in vendor_kernel_boot
records.summary: For the listed Pixel 7-and-later kernel-development targets, AOSP documents a split between vendor_boot and vendor_kernel_boot, with kernel artifacts contained by vendor_kernel_boot. Their kernel set also includes boot, dtbo, vendor_dlkm, and system_dlkm; Pixel 6-family instructions are not interchangeable.
symptoms: A Pixel 7-or-later kernel guide references vendor_boot instead of vendor_kernel_boot
Factory or kernel package contains vendor_kernel_boot
Kernel boots incompletely after only boot was replaced
diagnostic_steps: Confirm the exact Pixel codename and compare it with the source's listed kernel partition table.
Inventory boot, dtbo, vendor_kernel_boot, vendor_dlkm, system_dlkm, and vendor_boot without changing them.
Verify that all candidate images come from one supported platform and kernel combination.
fix_steps: Follow the exact model and kernel-branch guide whose partition list matches Device DNA.
Restore the complete coherent factory set when a Pixel 6-family or unrelated partition recipe was used.
expected_outcomes: Kernel artifacts and DLKM partitions match the documented Pixel generation layout.
known_incompatibility: Pixel 6 oriole
Pixel 6 Pro raven
Pixel 6a bluejay
Unlisted future devices require a newly reviewed source
recovery_routes: Android Flash Tool or exact Pixel factory image restore

scope.scope_note: Official partition map for Pixel kernel-development targets listed by AOSP at review time. It does not automatically extend to unlisted future Pixels.
